text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand we are evaluating a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To begin, can you describe the specific symptoms you are observing, such as the onset of breathing difficulties and any associated signs like cyanosis or grunting?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the premature birth at 33 weeks, I suspect respiratory distress syndrome due to surfactant deficiency. Are you observing any signs of grunting, nasal flaring, or chest retractions in the infant?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those signs are classic for Respiratory Distress Syndrome in a preterm infant. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the severity, I will request a chest X-ray. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
